To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pion form factor Fπ(Q2), calculated in perturbative QED and perturbative QFD, depends on the scheme used to define the running coupling constant, αs(Q2), and the subtraction point, Q, and that the optimized result is scheme independent.
the order α2s corrections to the picon form factor are large (≈30% at Q2=4GeV2) and scheme dependent.
the optimized result for Fπ(Q2), which is the same as that obtained by Stevenson’s prescription, is scheme independent and is in good agreement with the experimental value.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics: 1. The calculation of the 0(β0) and 0(β1) terms of the pion form factor in the MOM and MS schemes.
the following questions: (1) What is the best scheme to calculate the form factor? (2) What is the optimal subtraction point? (3) What is the most reliable method to obtain the optimal result?
the following: (i) The order α2 corrections to the pπ(Q2) in the MS and the MOM scheme.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optimized perturbative result for the pion form factor is scheme and subtraction point dependent.
the optimized pion form factor Fπ(Q2)=1+1.6αs(Q2)+O(α2s(Q2))
the order α2s correction to the pion electromagnetic form factor is small and scheme dependent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the order α2s corrections to Fπ(Q2)/Fπ(Q2) can be reduced to a 5% effect by choosing the subtraction point Q2 = 0.8 GeV2 and using the definition of α2s in Eq. (4.3).
we find a value for Q2/Q2 of about 0.1 for the optimal subtraction point Q.
there is no scheme‐independent definition for the running coupling constant and the pion form factor in perturbative QED.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimized perturbation theory can be used to obtain the value of Q2Fπ in a scheme independent manner.
the optimized result for Fπ is very sensitive to the definition of α(Q2).
the order α2s correction to Fπ is small and that the scheme dependence of the result can be removed by optimizing the perturbative result with respect to the subtraction point Q.
